Section 173(1) Of The Motor Vehicles Act, Praying

COMPENSATION AMOUNT BY RS.14,69,000/- ONLY, AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C M JOSHI  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE C M JOSHI)
1. Heard both the sides.
2. With consent of both the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal though it is slated for admission.

3. This appeal by the petitioner-claimant is directed against the judgment and award dated 05.07.2018 passed in NC: 2025:KHC-K:101 MVC Mo.908/2014 on the file of the Court of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT, Kalaburagi, (for short 'Tribunal'), seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant has raised two aspects to contend that the impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.908/2014 dated 05.07.2018 is erroneous.
The first prong of the arguments is that the Tribunal has not considered the amputation of the left thumb of the appellant in assessing the compensation.

The second submission by learned counsel for the appellant is that the Tribunal has fastened the liability on the owner of the vehicle though the owner Allauddin S/O Syed Sab Chincholi vs Gundayya And Anr on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12263492/
2 of the vehicle who is respondent No.1 had contested the matter, therefore, by applying the principles of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of PAPPU DEO YADAV VERSUS NARESH KUMAR AND ORS.1, the Tribunal should have ordered payment of the compensation at the first instance by the Insurance Company and then liberty should have been given to it to recover the same from the owner.

sentences.text: AIR 2020 SUPREME COURT 4424 NC: 2025:KHC-K:101 5.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company would submit that the Tribunal has rightly considered the medical records and came to the conclusion that there was no such amputation of the left thumb in the accident, though such evidence was led in the form of the opinion by the Medical Officer, who had assessed the disability only and not the treated Doctor.
Therefore, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company defends the impugned judgment.

6. Secondly, it is fairly submitted that the principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of 'PAPPU DEO YADAV' referred supra is squarely applicable to the case on hand and therefore, the Insurance Company has to be directed to pay the compensation, with liberty to recover the same from the owner thereafter.
7.
The perusal of the records would show that the petitioner claims that he had suffered an accident on 15.01.2013 while he was working as a Cleaner in Maxi cab bearing No.KA-17/3716.

When the driver of the Maxi cab NC: 2025:KHC-K:101 had applied the brake, it turned turtle and the petitioner had sustained injuries like fracture over the distal phalanx of the left thumb, lumbar region, dorsum of the right elbow, etc.
The Tribunal in its judgment notices the Wound Certificate produced at Ex.P6, which indicates that there was only an injury to the left thumb, but not the amputation.
However, the Tribunal also notices that the disability stated by PW2 is on the basis of an alleged amputation.

Obviously, the disability was assessed by PW2 at much later date than the date of the accident, therefore, the Tribunal opined that the amputation of the left thumb is not relatable to the accident, which had occurred on 15.01.2013, and accordingly held that the injury being simple in nature and awarded a global compensation of Rs.31,000/- including medical expenses at Rs.6,000/- as per medical bills.
8. It is worth to note that the petitioner in order to relate the amputation of the left thumb has not produced the case-sheet of the hospital.
Moreover, the Discharge Summary issued by the hospital also does not mention anything about amputation of the left thumb.

In the NC: 2025:KHC-K:101 absence of any mention of the amputation in Wound Certificate, Discharge Summary and Case-Sheet, it is not possible to accept the contention that the testimony of the PW2 would establish the amputation due to the injuries suffered in the accident.
Therefore, no indulgence can be made in such finding of the Tribunal.
9. Insofar as quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, it appears that injury is stated to be simple in nature, because there was no such discernible gravity to it.

Though,
there is a fracture of the phalanx, it was opined to be simple in nature.
In other words, the injury falls in between the simple and the grievous one, but there being no amputation it was opined to be simple.

However, considering these aspects, it would be just and proper to award a sum of Allauddin S/O Syed Sab Chincholi vs Gundayya And Anr on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12263492/
3 Rs.15,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In view of the fact that respondent No.1 had appeared before the Tribunal and had contested the matter, the dispute between respondent Nos.1 and 2 as to whether NC: 2025:KHC-K:101 the driver of the vehicle had a valid driving license or not is a matter to be decided amongst themselves, which is in the realm of terms and conditions.

But when respondent No.1 has appeared before the Tribunal and filed his written statement, it would be proper to direct respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to pay the compensation and then recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

Hence the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The appellant is entitled for an additional sum of Rs.15,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

iii) The 2nd respondent - Insurance Company is directed to pay the compensation amount within 8 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the 1st respondent - owner of the vehicle.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:101 iv) Entire amount ordered herein is to be released to the petitioner.

Sd/-
